en.name: Siricius
en.summary: The first pope known to have issued a formal papal decretal, addressing questions of clerical discipline with the force of law.
en.body: Siricius is credited with the earliest surviving papal decretal, a letter to a Spanish bishop answering questions on clerical celibacy, penance, and baptism in a tone of binding legal authority rather than mere advice — a significant step in the development of formal papal governance. His reign also saw continued disputes over the legacy of the theologian Jovinian, whom Siricius condemned for downplaying the value of celibacy and asceticism.
